editions.text:
The station recorded 116 feeder visits and 19 species, marking a noticeably quieter day compared to the weekly average of 230 visits. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees remained the dominant regulars, holding steady with 63 and 14 confident visits respectively. This drop in traffic distinguishes the day from the heavier counts seen earlier in the week, where visits consistently exceeded 200.

Species composition stayed consistent with recent patterns, as thirteen regulars were recorded on all seven days. Broad-winged Hawk and Song Sparrow appeared for the first time this week, while Red-shouldered Hawk and White-eyed Vireo were absent. No new audio equipment or feeder changes occurred to explain these shifts in detection.

The day closed with a Tufted Titmouse observed twenty-one minutes before sunset. Carolina Wrens and Gray Catbirds provided a steady presence in the final hours, rounding out the total of 16 species heard. The overall picture remains one of routine activity, simply at a lower volume than the previous week.
